questions.question: Which of the following states has two houses in its state legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A legislature with two houses, or chambers.**
 
• The British parliament is a** bicameral legislature, made up of the House of Commons and the House of Lords.**
 
• A bicameral system is a reference to a government with two legislative houses or chambers.
 
• **Bicameral is the Latin word that describes a two-house legislative system.**
 
• **The bicameral system originated in England, and the U.S. adopted that system upon its founding. **
 
• A bicameral system is a government style with two separate divisions within the legislative branch of government, versus a unicameral system that does not divide the government branch.
 
• In India, the two houses of the state legislature are –** Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council.**
 
• There are only six states which have two-tier of legislature –** Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 **Article 204**

questions.question: Which of the following is the only large river in the Indian desert?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Luni River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Luni River originates from Nag Pahar or Naga hills in the Ajmer district of Rajasthan.
 
• Luni originates in the Pushkar valley of the Aravalli Range, near Ajmer and passes through the southeastern portion of the Thar Desert.
 
• It is the only large river in the Indian desert.
 
• It ends in the marshy lands of Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.
 
• Luni River flows through the Ajmer, Barmer, Jalore, Jodhpur, Nagaur, Pali, and Sirohi districts of Rajasthan and the Banaskantha and Patan districts of Gujarat.
 
• Sukri, Mithri River, Bandi, Khari, Jawai, Guhiya and Sagi are the left-bank tributary of River Luni.
 
• Jojari is the right bank tributary of River Luni.
 
• Jaswant Sagar Dam was built in 1892 by Maharaja Jaswant Singh and is one of the largest artificial lakes in India.
 
• Sardar Samand and Jawai dam are major irrigation projects on River Luni.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Betwa River

 
 
• It is also known as Betravati and Vetravati, which is a major river in India.
 
• Originates from Kumra Gao (Gohar Ganj Tehsil) of Raisen and flows into Vidisha
 
• During its total course of 590 km, the Betwa river passes through the states of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Rivers are the lifelines of human establishments.
 
• They provide us with water and fertile lands. Civilizations have always settled on the banks of rivers.
 
• Betwa also passes through many major cities and districts including, Vidisha, Sanchi, and Orchha.
 
• It empties in the Yamuna river in Hamirpur, Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• The Kosi:
 
 
• It is an antecedent river with its source to the north of Mount Everest in Tibet, where its mainstream Arun rises.
 
• After crossing the Central Himalayas in Nepal, it is joined by the Son Kosi from the West and the Tamur Kosi from the east.
 
• It forms Sapt Kosi after uniting with the river Arun.
 
 
 
• **Banas river:**
 
 
• Banas river originates from Khamnor Hills of the Aravalli Range, near Kumbhalgarh in Rajsamand, Rajasthan. '
 
• Banas river is a tributary of the Chambal River and it is approximately 512 kilometres in length.
 
• This river is also called ‘Van Ki Asha‘.
 
• There is another river in Rajasthan with the name of Banas.
 
• The Banas river entirely flows within Rajasthan in:-
 
 
• Ajmer, Bhilwara, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Dausa, Jaipur, Pali, Rajsamand, Sawai Madhopur, Sirohi, Tonk, and Udaipur districts of Rajasthan. 
 
 
 
• It flows northeast through the Mewar region of Rajasthan and meets the Chambal near the village of Rameshwar in Sawai Madhopur district.

questions.question: Aihole was the capital of the __ __.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Chalukyas.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The capital of the **Chalukyas was Aihole.**
 
• Aihole in **Karnataka state, India, is known as the Cradle of Indian architecture.**
 
• It was the first capital of Chalukyas where they built numerous temples dating back to the 6th century.
 
• The Hindu temples at Aihole reflect a "meeting and fragmentation of styles".
 
• The early temples at Aihole may also be a window into the more ancient Indian society.**​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Chalukya Dynasty​

 
 
• ​It lasted from 543 A.D. to 755 A.D.
 
• Pulakeshin I was the founder of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
• **Pulakeshin I took Vatapi the modern-day Badami in Bagalkot district, Karnataka under his control and made it his capital later.**
 
• Kirtivarman II was the last of the rulers of the Chalukyas.
 
• He was defeated by Dantidurga, the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty.

questions.question: Who among the following devised the policy 'Doctrine of Lapse'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Lord Dalhousie__.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The doctrine of Lapse:

 
 
• Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse for annexing the dependant states whose ruler died without a natural heir to succeed him.
 
• Some important Indian States viz. Satara (1848), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (**1849**), and Nagpur (1854) were annexed by the enforcement of the Doctrine of Lapse
 
 
 
• Lord Dalhousie:
 
 
• In 1848, Lord Dalhousie arrived in India as the Governor-General and was determined to extend British rule over India.
 
• Dalhousie occupied the Punjab and Sindh through war and brought several subordinate states directly under the Company’s rule by annexing them on the basis of the Doctrine of Lapse. 
 
• Lord Dalhousie also introduced the Doctrine of Good of Governed under which Awadh (1856) and Punjab (1849) were annexed.
 
• Dalhousie established Public Works Department, the objective behind the formation of this department was the construction and maintenance of canals, roads, bridges, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Mountbatten:**

 
 
• He was the last British viceroy of India and he was appointed by the British government to wrap up the British Empire in our country. 
 
• He served as the last Viceroy of India from February 12, 1947, to August 15, 1947, and then as the first Governor-General of free India from August 15, 1947, to June 21, 1948.
 
• On June 3, 1947, Lord Mountbatten put forward his plan which outlined the steps for the solution to India's political problem.
 
• The main purpose of the Mountbatten Plan was the partition of India and the speedy transfer of responsibility, initially in the form of Dominion Status.
 
 
 
• 
 Lord Cornwallis:

 
 
 
• Lord Cornwallis was the Governor-General of Fort William (Bengal) and the Commander-in-Chief of British India. 
 
• The Third Anglo-Mysore War took place in his tenure.
 
• Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal and other parts of India.
 
• He established thanas to maintain law and order.
 
• He founded a Sanskrit College at Benaras for Hindus and this is today the Government Sanskrit College in Benares.
 
• He also established a mint at Calcutta.
 
 
 
 
• Lord Canning:
 
 
• Lord Canning served as Governor-General of India from 1856 to 1862.
 
• During his tenure, the Government of India Act, 1858 was passed which created the office of Viceroy to be held by the same person who was Governor-General of India.
 
• Thus, Lord Canning also served as the first Viceroy of India.
 
• The Mutiny of 1857, which he was able to suppress successfully,
 
• The Passing of the Indian Councils Act, 1861 which introduced a portfolio system in India,
 
• Bengal Rent Act (1859).

questions.concept: Ecology and Functions of an ecosystem
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of artificial ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Garden**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Artificial Ecosystem

 
 
• An artificial ecosystem meets all the requirements of a natural ecosystem but is made and controlled by humans.
 
• It is made to mimic a natural ecosystem but often is less complex and with a very low genetic diversity.
 
• Orchards, farmlands, a garden, and man-made reservoirs are some different varieties of artificial ecosystems.
 
• Humans need to slouch each factor of the artificial ecosystem to make it a sustainable environment.
 
• A paddy field postulates fertilizers and a consistent supply of water in order to grow crops.
 
• When the crops are harvested, it leaves the farm an open system that pivots external sources in order for new plants and organic matter to develop and thrive.
 
• A garden needs to be tended by pulling out weeds and dislodging parasites through chemical or organic fertilizers.
 
• Small rodents, insects, and birds can also outlive in the garden and provide biodiversity, but humans drive away most of these animals to maintain the equilibrium of the garden.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ecosystem:

 
 
• An ecosystem can be visualised as a functional unit of nature, where living organisms (producers, consumers, and decomposers) interact among themselves and also with the surrounding physical environment.
 
• An ecosystem can be of any size but usually encompasses specific and limited species.
 
• E.g. Aquatic Ecosystem. (This is how the ecosystem is different from Environment).
 
• Rice is a staple food of not only India but over half of the world population.
 
• Over 3 billion people consume cereal every day.
 
• However, it is also one of the most water-intensive crops.
 
 

 
• Forest:

 
 
• Forest, a complex ecological system in which trees are the dominant life-form.
 
• Tree-dominated forests can occur wherever the temperatures rise above 10 °C (50 °F) in the warmest months and the annual precipitation is more than 200 mm (8 inches).
 
• They can develop under a variety of conditions within these climatic limits, and the kind of soil, plant, and animal life differs according to the extremes of environmental influences.
 
 
 
• Grassland:
 
 
• Grassland, area in which the vegetation is dominated by a nearly continuous cover of grasses.
 
• Grasslands occur in environments conducive to the growth of this plant cover but not to that of taller plants, particularly trees and shrubs.
 
• The factors preventing the establishment of such taller, woody vegetation are varied.
 
 
 
• Lake:
 
 
• Lake, any relatively large body of slowly moving or standing water that occupies an inland basin of appreciable size.
 
• Definitions that precisely distinguish lakes, ponds, swamps, and even rivers and other bodies of nonoceanic water are not well established.
 
• It may be said, however, that rivers and streams are relatively fast moving; marshes and swamps contain relatively large quantities of grasses, trees, or shrubs; and ponds are relatively small in comparison with lakes.

questions.question: Which of the following substances is insoluble in water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalk Powder**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Calcium Carbonate is the carbonic salt of calcium (CaCO3).
 
• Calcium Carbonate (also known as chalk), mined as calcite, is the most commonly used filler for PVC.
 
• Calcium Carbonate is insoluble in water because the electrostatic bonds between the carbonate anion and the calcium ion are too strong to be overcome by solvation by water molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**

 
• It is the chemical name for salt.
 
• Sodium is an electrolyte that regulates the amount of water in your body.
 
• Soluble in: Water, Ammonia, Methanol, Glycerol, Formic acid, Propylene glycol, Formamide.

**Lithium Bromide (LiBr)**

 
• It is a lithium salt in which the counterion is bromide.
 
• The anhydrous salt forms cubic crystals are similar to common salt.
 
• It is soluble in water, alcohol, and ether.
 
• It is prepared by the action of hydrobromic acid on lithium hydroxide.

**Magnesium Iodide (MgI2)**

 
• It is typical ionic halides, being highly soluble in water.

questions.question: How many fundamental duties of Indian citizens are there in the Indian Constitution, as of March 2022?
At which Buddhist site of India did Gautama Buddha first preach the Dharma?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarnath**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first sermon was delivered to his 5 disciples at Sarnath in a deer park.
 
• The first sermon delivered by Buddha was on deliverance from suffering.
 
• The event of the first sermon is known as "Dharmachakra Pravartana" which means turning the wheel of dharma.
 
• In the first sermon, Buddha gave two elements of the Holy Trinity of Buddhism.
 
 
• Dhamma: Teachings
 
• Sangha: Order of Buddhist monks and nuns
 
 
 
• His five disciples became Arhats.
 
• Buddha obtained Mahaparinirvana at the age of 80 in Kushinagar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• After attaining Enlightenment Buddha discovered four noble truths:

 
 
• The truth of suffering (Dukkha)
 
• The truth of the cause of suffering (Samudaya)
 
• The truth of the end of suffering (Nirodha), and
 
• The truth of the path that leads to the end of suffering (Astangika-Marga).
 
 
 
• Buddha attained Enlightenment at the age of 35 at Gaya under a Peepal tree at Uruvela.
 
• The Peepal tree under which Buddha attained Enlightenment is the famous Bodhi tree.

questions.question: Sam talks about an example of an igneous rock. Which of the following can it be?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Basalt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are many different kinds of rocks which are grouped under three families on the basis of their mode of formation. They are: -
 
• Igneous Rocks - Igneous rock is formed through the cooling and solidification of magma or lava. The magma can be derived from partial melts of existing rocks in either a planet's mantle or crust.
 
 
• ​The two main categories of igneous rocks are extrusive and intrusive
 
 
• Extrusive rocks__ are formed on the surface of the Earth from lava, which is magma that has emerged from underground. example-pumice, obsidian, andesite, rhyolite, and basalt.
 
• __Intrusive rocks __are formed from magma that cools and solidifies within the crust of the planet. example-Diorite, granite, pegmatite.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Sedimentary Rocks — Sedimentary rocks are types of rock that are formed by the accumulation or deposition of mineral or organic particles at Earth's surface, followed by cementation. example-sandstone, limestone, and shale.
 
• Metamorphic Rocks —Metamorphic rocks arise from the transformation of existing rock to new types of rock, in a process called metamorphism. example- phyllite, schist, gneiss, quartzite and marble.​

questions.question: The financial year in the Indian economy runs from __ __.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 April to 31 March**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Financial Year-

 
 
• In India, it runs from 1st April of a year to 31st March__ of the next upcoming year.
 
• It guides the creation of the government's budget, financial regulations, and financial policies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Budget-

 
 
• The primary budget document for our government is contained in the Annual Financial Statement.
 
• The annual financial statement prepared by the government, which is initiated by the legislature and approved by the president or chief executive, shows the revenues and expenses for a certain fiscal year.
 
• India's finance minister presented the financial budget.
 
 

 
• The practice of a separate Railway Budget was started by the British in 1924.
 
• On 21 September 2016, the Government of India approved the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union budget of India and thus came to the end of the 92-year-old practice of separate rail and general budgets.

questions.question: Which of the following trains of India is the fastest (as per trial runs), as of April 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vande Bharat Express (Train 18)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vande Bharat Express is an Indian high-speed intercity electric multiple unit train.
 
• It was designed and built by Integral Coach Factory (ICF) at Perambur, Chennai under the Indian government's Make in India initiative over a span of 18 months. 
 
• During trials, it attained a maximum speed of 180km/hr.
 
• The actual top speed is restricted to 130 km/hr due to the speed limit of the railway track of routes, which are used by Vande Bharat Express.
 
• Vande Bharat has an air-conditioned chair car service with 16 coaches.
 
• It is an engine-less self-propelled train set that allows for faster acceleration and deceleration.
 
• Vande Bharat Express operates five days a week except on Monday and Thursday and covers the distance between New Delhi and Varanasi in eight hours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The " Integral Coach Factory, Chennai" was established on 2nd October 1955.
 
• It is located in Perumbur, Chennai, Tamil Nadu.
 
• The construction of this factory was initiated by Cheif Minister K. Kamaraj.
 
• It is one of the four rake production units of the Indian railway after -

 
• Modern Coach Factory, Raebareli.
 
• Rail Coach Factory, Kapurthala
 
• Marathwada rail coach factory, Latur.
